subsystems.name: Airframe and propulsion
subsystems.role: carries a few kilograms of payload and hovers or cruises to the drop point.

subsystems.name: Autonomy stack
subsystems.role: flies the route and avoids other aircraft and obstacles without a human at the controls.
parts: flight controller with redundant inertial sensors
lidar, radar and cameras for detect-and-avoid
onboard computer running routing and contingency logic

subsystems.name: Communications mesh
subsystems.role: keeps each aircraft linked to the fleet and to air-traffic systems.
parts: cellular or 5G modem for beyond-line-of-sight links

subsystems.name: Traffic management layer
subsystems.role: keeps many aircraft separated from each other and from crewed aviation.

subsystems.name: Ground infrastructure
subsystems.role: launches, recovers, charges and reloads aircraft.

subsystems.name: Fleet orchestration
subsystems.role: assigns each job to an aircraft and re-plans when wind, demand or airspace closures change.

buildSteps.title: Map the corridor and clear the regulation
buildSteps.detail: Survey the route, model obstacles and population density, and obtain the airspace authorisation that allows flight beyond the pilot's line of sight.

buildSteps.title: Design the airframe for the payload
buildSteps.detail: Choose multirotor for hover-and-lower delivery or a fixed-wing or hybrid design for longer range; size the battery around the required payload, range and headwind margin.

buildSteps.title: Build the flight controller and sense-and-avoid
buildSteps.detail: Fuse inertial, GNSS and barometric data for state estimation, then add lidar, radar or stereo cameras so the aircraft can detect conflicting traffic and self-separate.

buildSteps.title: Integrate communications and identity
buildSteps.detail: Install redundant command links, a cellular or 5G modem, and a remote-identification broadcast so the aircraft is visible to authorities and other airspace users.

buildSteps.title: Connect to the traffic-management layer
buildSteps.detail: Register the fleet with the UTM or U-space service, load geofences, and test conflict detection against simulated traffic.

buildSteps.title: Set up ground nests
buildSteps.detail: Place docks with charging, payload handling and weather covers along the route, sized so turnaround is minutes and battery cycling is within limits.

buildSteps.title: Test incrementally, then certify
buildSteps.detail: Fly line-of-sight, then extended visual line-of-sight, then beyond-line-of-sight, accumulating reliability data needed for operational approval.

buildSteps.title: Operate as a mesh
buildSteps.detail: Run many aircraft under one supervising team, with dynamic re-routing and shared separation so density, not range, becomes the limit.

prerequisites.why: most regulators only allow it case by case or in approved corridors, which caps fleet scale.
reliable, certified avoidance of uncooperative aircraft is still maturing and is the main safety barrier.
4G and 5G give command-and-control coverage in cities; 6G is not needed for today's operations.
today's packs give a few kilograms over tens of kilometres; range and cold-weather performance remain limiting.
these are being deployed region by region and their rules are not yet globally harmonised.

pathway.milestone: beyond-line-of-sight medical and parcel routes in approved corridors — blood and vaccine delivery in Rwanda began in 2016, and suburban parcel delivery in Australia followed in 2019
pathway.unlocks: operational experience and safety data for routine remote flight.

pathway.milestone: certified detect-and-avoid and remote identification in routine urban operations
pathway.unlocks: operations that no longer need a visual observer or a segregated corridor.

pathway.milestone: one supervisor managing many aircraft in a shared mesh, with automatic conflict resolution
pathway.unlocks: density: more deliveries per hour from the same airspace and ground infrastructure.

pathway.milestone: full integration with crewed aviation, and urban monitoring and emergency response sharing the same airspace
pathway.unlocks: drone logistics treated as ordinary infrastructure rather than an experiment.
